comparison.rationale: Fast, strong baseline for count/TF-IDF features. Very interpretable: each word contributes an additive log-probability.
comparison.notes: Assumes word independence - a simplification, but it works well on short SMS.

comparison.rationale: Linear decision boundary works well for high-dimensional sparse TF-IDF; gives calibrated probabilities and per-word coefficients we can explain.
comparison.notes: Probabilities are the model's confidence, not a guarantee about a specific message.

comparison.rationale: Non-linear ensemble that can capture interactions between words (e.g. 'free' + 'call' + 'now'). Useful as a contrast to linear models.
comparison.notes: Slower, larger artefact, and less interpretable per prediction than LR.

selection_reason: LogisticRegression: spam F1 0.9407, precision 0.9520, recall 0.9297, ROC-AUC 0.9985 on the held-out test set; 5-fold CV F1 0.9372 +/- 0.0116. It is statistically tied on F1 with RandomForest, MultinomialNB (gap < 0.01, smaller than the CV fold spread), so the tie-break was ROC-AUC (0.9985) and then model simplicity.
limitations: English SMS only. Hindi/Hinglish text is NOT reliably classified by this model; those messages rely on the curated rule engine.
Minority class (12.4% spam): accuracy alone is misleading, so F1/recall are reported.
The output probability is a model score, not a guarantee of fraud or safety.
